b: Five poems over the ruin of Jerusalem, four of them acrostics. The formality is not coldness; it is grief given a container so it can be borne. At the exact centre sit the verses about mercies new every morning — hope, surrounded on both sides by devastation.

3.t: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases — placed at the exact centre of five poems about the destruction of Jerusalem, surrounded on both sides by devastation.

1.t: Look and see if there is any sorrow like mine. Read on Good Friday for obvious reasons.

5.t: The book ends without resolution: unless you have utterly rejected us. Scripture permits an unresolved ending.

2.t: The most unflinching chapter in Lamentations, describing God himself as the destroyer. Scripture does not flatten grief into comfort.

4.h: The gold has lost its lustre
4.t: Starving children and mothers in desperation. The horror of the siege recorded without softening. Worth talking through with a pastor or a mature Christian you trust.
